notYet: Not yet part of Iberia, Gaul and Italy

stages.name: Gallic & Alpine tribes
stages.desc: Independent Celtic, Ligurian and Alpine peoples; some fought Hannibal, others joined him

stages.name: Carthaginian-held
stages.desc: Barcid Iberia: Carthage's empire in Spain, ruled from New Carthage

stages.name: On the march route
stages.desc: Lands Hannibal's army fought or bargained its way across in 218 BC

stages.name: Roman-controlled
stages.desc: Rome, its colonies and its Italian allies

stages.name: Roman lands invaded
stages.desc: Roman territory with Hannibal's army inside it and the Po Gauls in revolt

states.name: France
timeline: Celtic peoples (Volcae, Allobroges, Cavares and many more) and Greek Massalia, Rome's ally, on the coast
Hannibal crosses Gaul from the Pyrenees to the Rhône and up into the Alps, fighting the Volcae and the Allobroges

states.name: Spain
timeline: Hasdrubal the Fair rules Barcid Iberia from New Carthage; a treaty of 226 BC bars him from crossing the Ebro in arms
Hasdrubal is murdered; the army acclaims Hannibal, aged about twenty-six, and attacks the Olcades
Hannibal raids the Vaccaei as far as Salamanca and routs the Carpetani on the Tagus
Saguntum, a friend of Rome, falls after an eight-month siege
Hannibal marches north; his brother Hasdrubal holds Iberia, while Gnaeus Scipio lands at Emporion

states.name: Italy
timeline: Roman Italy, with Sicily and Sardinia; a Gallic army invading from the Po valley is destroyed at Telamon
Rome conquers the Insubres; the Po valley Gauls submit
Hannibal descends into the Po valley, wins at the Ticinus and the Trebia, and the Gauls rise to join him

states.name: Switzerland
timeline: Celtic and Alpine peoples of the high valleys, outside the reach of Rome or Carthage
Hannibal's route lies to the south-west, over the passes between Gaul and the Po valley

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal the Fair governs Carthage's Iberian empire from New Carthage, the harbour city he founded a few years earlier.

events.title: The Ebro line
events.text: Under a treaty agreed with Rome in 226 BC, Hasdrubal has pledged not to cross the Ebro in arms.

events.title: Battle of Telamon
events.text: Two Roman armies trap and destroy a great Gallic army of Boii, Insubres and Gaesatae on the Tuscan coast.

events.title: The Boii submit
events.text: Roman consuls march into the lands of the Boii around Bologna and force them to submit.

events.title: Flaminius crosses the Po
events.text: The consul Gaius Flaminius invades the country of the Insubres and defeats them near the Adda.

events.title: Clastidium
events.text: Marcus Claudius Marcellus kills the Gallic king Viridomarus in single combat.

events.title: Mediolanum falls
events.text: Rome takes Milan, the chief town of the Insubres; the Po valley is under Roman control.

events.title: Hasdrubal murdered
events.text: Hasdrubal is assassinated; the army acclaims Hannibal, son of Hamilcar, about twenty-six years old.

events.title: War on the Olcades
events.text: In his first campaign, Hannibal storms the Olcades' chief town on the central plateau.

events.title: Helmantica
events.text: Hannibal raids the Vaccaei far to the north-west, taking Helmantica, today's Salamanca.

events.title: Battle of the Tagus
events.text: Ambushed at the river by the Carpetani, he crushes them with his cavalry and elephants.

events.title: Via Flaminia
events.text: In Italy, Flaminius builds a great road north from Rome to Ariminum, toward the Gallic frontier.

events.title: Siege of Saguntum
events.text: Hannibal besieges Saguntum, a city under Rome's protection; he is wounded by a javelin at its walls.

events.title: War in Illyria
events.text: Rome sends both consuls across the Adriatic against Demetrius of Pharos, not to Iberia.

events.title: Saguntum falls
events.text: After eight months the city falls; its wealth pays Hannibal's army.

events.title: War declared
events.text: At Carthage, the Roman envoy Fabius offers peace or war from a fold of his toga; the Carthaginians accept war.

events.title: Vows at Gades
events.text: Before the march, Hannibal makes vows at the temple of Melqart at Gades.

events.title: The march begins
events.text: In late spring Hannibal leaves New Carthage with some ninety thousand foot, twelve thousand horse and his elephants.

events.title: Crossing the Ebro
events.text: The army crosses the Ebro, the line in Hasdrubal's treaty with Rome.

events.title: Hanno holds Catalonia
events.text: Hannibal conquers the Ilergetes and their neighbours with heavy losses and leaves Hanno with eleven thousand men.

events.title: Over the Pyrenees
events.text: After sending some troops home, he crosses the Pyrenees with fifty thousand foot and nine thousand horse.

events.title: Ruscino
events.text: Gallic chiefs meet Hannibal near Perpignan and, won over with gifts, let the army pass.

events.title: Placentia founded
events.text: Rome plants colonies of six thousand settlers each at Placentia and Cremona on the Po.

events.title: The Boii rise
events.text: The Boii and Insubres attack the new colonies and drive Roman officials into Mutina.

events.title: Scipio at Massalia
events.text: The consul Publius Cornelius Scipio lands near Massalia, expecting to meet Hannibal in Iberia.

events.title: Hanno's night march
events.text: Hanno, son of Bomilcar, crosses the Rhône upstream at night and signals with smoke.

events.title: Crossing the Rhône
events.text: The army crosses in boats and dugouts as Hanno falls on the Gauls defending the far bank.

events.title: Elephants on rafts
events.text: The elephants are ferried on rafts covered with earth; some leap into the river, but all 37 reach the far bank.

events.title: Cavalry clash
events.text: Five hundred Numidian horsemen and three hundred Roman cavalry meet in a bloody skirmish by the Rhône.

events.title: Gnaeus to Iberia
events.text: Arriving three days too late, Scipio sends his army to Iberia under his brother Gnaeus, who lands at Emporion.

events.title: The Island
events.text: Where the Isère meets the Rhône, Hannibal settles a royal quarrel and receives grain, weapons and warm clothing.

events.title: Allobroges ambush
events.text: At the start of the climb the Allobroges hold the heights; Hannibal seizes them by night but loses many pack animals.

events.title: The white rock
events.text: A tribe bearing olive branches offers guides, then attacks in a gorge; Hannibal spends the night by a bare white rock.

events.title: Snow on the summit
events.text: On the ninth day the army reaches the pass as the first snow falls; Hannibal points to the plains of Italy.

events.title: The rockfall
events.text: On the descent a landslide has carried away the path; the men rebuild it, and Livy tells of rock split with fire and vinegar.

events.title: Col de la Traversette
events.text: A high pass of 2,947 metres; in 2016 a peat bog below it yielded a churned layer of animal dung dated to around 218 BC.

events.title: Col du Clapier
events.text: A pass of about 2,480 metres favoured by many modern scholars, with a view down toward the Italian plain.

events.title: Mont Cenis
events.text: A broad, lower pass that Napoleon believed was Hannibal's road.

events.title: Little St Bernard
events.text: The pass preferred by many nineteenth-century scholars, leading down to the Aosta valley.

events.title: Taurini stormed
events.text: Hannibal takes the chief town of the Taurini, near today's Turin, in three days.

events.title: Battle of the Ticinus
events.text: Hannibal's Numidian cavalry routs Scipio's horsemen; the wounded consul is rescued, by one account, by his son.

events.title: Battle of the Trebia
events.text: In December, the consul Sempronius is lured across the icy river and his army is destroyed.

events.title: The elephants die
events.text: In the cold after the Trebia, all but one of the elephants perish.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's Spain, France, Switzerland and Italy, each country coloured by who held most of it, or what happened there, by the end of each year. A strong simplification: Barcid Iberia never ruled the whole peninsula, Roman Italy included the Gauls of the Po valley only from 222 BC, and in 218 BC control changed month by month. Regions are today's boundaries; the route over the Alps is still disputed.
